name: Name
body: The Black Tide campaign follows the return of the Orgoth to the shores of the Iron Kingdoms for the first time in 400 years, from the arrival of the first vanguard to pushing the defenders back to their mightiest cities. A dark future hangs over the Iron Kingdoms—will you stand firm against the invasion, or will you join it and revel in the spoils of war?

name: Name
body: Black Tide is an ongoing campaign for two or more players. The campaign takes place over four seasons, with each season comprised of three chapters, delivered one chapter per month via subscription to the WARMACHINE app. Each chapter is comprised of three scenarios. When playing the Black Tide campaign, each player will choose to play as either an Invader or a Defender. If players select the same allegiance, it will be necessary for players to play games of the opposing allegiance in order to facilitate all players having the opportunity to play through the three scenarios according to their chosen allegiance. Players should divide themselves between Invaders and Defenders as evenly as possible. Scenarios are intended to be played in order but can be repeated for campaign groups of more than two players in order to allow all players to play each scenario in the role of their chosen allegiance. It is not necessary for all players to play each other, only that all players have the opportunity to play each scenario. Players should only gain War Chest points (see below) from their best result of a specific scenario each season. So, if a player repeats a scenario, only record the results of the highest score for that scenario; do not record the points from a specific scenario more than once.

name: Name
body: Over the course of the campaign, players will track War Chest points to determine their success in the campaign. War Chest points are gained based on the outcome of scenario battles. Each player will be responsible to keep a tally of their own War Chest points. At the end of the third chapter, a player’s War Chest total will be used to rate that player’s performance as either an Invader of the Iron Kingdoms or as one of its valiant Defenders. War Chest points are awarded as follows: -Playing a Campaign Game: 1 point -Winning a Key Battle: +1 point -Winning by Killing the Opposing Leader: +1 point -Winning by Scenario Victory Conditions: +2 points

name: Name
body: Black Tide campaign scenarios are intended to be played in order. Each scenario grants the winning player, either the Invader or the Defender, an advantage in the subsequent scenario. Advantages are one-use only and can only be used the first time the winning player plays the scenario that follows the scenario in which the advantage was awarded.

name: Name
body: When setting up to play Black Tide scenarios, players will take turns placing terrain on the table as described by the scenario. When placing terrain features, a player cannot place an obstacle or obstruction within 5" of another obstacle or obstruction.

name: Name
body: Due to the nature of these scenarios, with the Invader sometimes striking the Defender without warning from sea or under the cover of darkness, the Invading player will not be allowed to place Defenses in same cases. It will be noted in the Terrain Placement section of each scenario whether the Invader can place Defenses or not.

name: Name
body: A flag is a scenario marker on a 40 mm base. A flag, however, is not a model. Models cannot end their movement on flags or be placed on them for any reason. A model can move through a flag if it has enough movement to move completely past it. While playing a Black Tide scenario, a player controls a flag when one or more of non-Cohort models are B2B with the flag and none of their opponent’s models contest it. A flag is contested if one or more of your opponent’s models are within 4" of it. Inert warjacks and wild warbeasts cannot contest flags.

name: Name
body: Some Black Tide scenarios are designated as key battles. These are particularly large or important battles to the narrative of the campaign. Key Battle scenarios are noted in the title of the scenario. A player who wins a Key Battle gains an additional War Chest point.

name: Name
body:
<i>The staccato rhythm of metal clicking against metal filled the command tent, ominous and urgent in its cryptic tapping. It was echoed by the quiet scratch of the wire scribe’s pen against paper, copying each letter as it came through the line, switching it with the appropriate character on the encryption key, and adding each word to the parchment before him.
Behind him, straddling a weather-worn trunk, the scribe’s battle sergeant tapped his foot idly, mumbling in a gruff voice. "They’ll send us west, that’ll be it. Join up with Gregor and the 2nd Garrison. Cash in on that keg he owes us, yeah?"
Kommandant Belov remained silent in response, her slow pacing wearing a faint line in the rug beneath her. She had not said a word since the message began to arrive, and now the excruciating wait for its completion was coming to a close.
The clicking fell silent. The wire scribe finished scribbling the final characters, hesitating with his pen just off the paper as his eyes finally took in the entirety of the missive. He half-turned on his stool, lifting the paper toward his commander.

name: Name
body:
"Kommandant."
The edge of the paper fluttered softly in the quiet tent. The scribe’s hand was shaking.
Belov plucked the parchment from his fingers and nodded once, dismissing the boy. "Go get some food, Privat." Her keen eyes darted across the page in quick lines, but she said nothing else. The battle sergeant leaned forward expectantly, but the lengthening quiet and the look in his kommandant’s eyes chilled him in a way the winter winds never did.
"Kommandant?" Silence.
"Mira?" His voice was quiet, the softest word he’d spoken in their two years commanding together.
Her lips moved quietly before the words began. "For immediate action. Break camp and move east. Secure the retreat—" She stopped, the word catching in her throat. "—secure the retreat of the 2nd Garrison."
"We’re falling back."
Her eyes kept moving, sweeping over the awful characters. "Evacuate civilians as able. Burn the bridges at Volsk. Leave nothing behind of use for the enemy."
She lowered the paper, her eyes distant, setting her jaw with a stare as cold and hard as the Motherland itself. "Salt the earth."

name: Name
body: <i>Among the column of soldiers, a weary band of civilian refugees shuffles along, clutching what possessions they were able to save in the chaos. Each one has the same prayer on their lips, hoping to reach safety before the invaders find their trail. Their fortune is not to be so, as war cries from the nearby hills rattle the convoy. The enemy has found them.

name: Name
body: In this scenario, the Defender attempt to escort civilian evacuees across the board while being attacked on both flanks by the Invader.

name: Name
body: Scenario 4 is suitable for 50-point armies.

name: Name
body:
The Defender’s deployment zone is centered on the board as shown on the map, 8" wide. The board edge that is opposite from the Defender’s deployment zone is designated the exit edge. During deployment, the Defender places seven 30 mm Civilian tokens within their deployment zone.
The Defender is the first player when playing this scenario.

name: Name
body: Players alternate placing terrain features, with each player placing up to 4 features. Neither player may place Defenses when playing this scenario. Terrain should not be placed between the Defender’s deployment zone and the exit board edge.

name: Name
body: -Civilians: On the Defender’s turn, the Defender can move each Civilian token not in base contact with an enemy model up to 6". The tokens may not pass over a model’s base while being moved and are affected by terrain. Civilian tokens in contact with an enemy model cannot move. -Escape or Capture: If a Civilian token ends its movement in contact with the exit board edge, it is removed. The Defender gains 1 War Chest point for each Civilian token removed in this way. The Invader gains 2 War Chest points for each Civilian token still on the board at the end of the sixth turn. -Surprise Attack: The Invader loses Ambush and Advance Deployment for this scenario.

name: Name
body:
Each player gains 1 War Chest point for playing the match.
A player immediately wins the match if that player controls the only Leader model in play. (the winning player gains +1 War Chest point)
At the end of the sixth turn, the player with the most War Chest points wins. (the winning player gains +2 War Chest points)

name: Name
body:
If the Invader player wins this match, when playing the next scenario, Scenario #5: Burn the Bridges, that player can choose two units to gain Ambush.
If the Defender player wins this match, when playing the next scenario, Scenario #5: Burn the Bridges, once during the game at the start of any of their Control Phases, that player can return up to two destroyed trooper models to a friendly unit. These models must be placed within 2" of another model in their unit. Models are returned with all of their damage boxes unmarked. A returned Grunt must forfeit its Normal Movement and Combat Actions the turn it is returned to play.

name: Name
body: <i>The drums grow louder on the horizon as blasting charges are thrust into eager hands and jaws are set, eyes steeling. The bridge over the shallow river spans high above. Once a monument to grand feats of engineering, it is now nothing more than one more desperate ploy to stall the invaders. The fuse is lit, and none may now escape the coming storm.

name: Name
body: In this scenario, the Defender races to bring down a bridge by destroying the supports with blasting charges while the Invader fights to keep their path inland intact.

name: Name
body: Scenario 5 is suitable for 7–100-point armies

name: Name
body:
Draw a line 12" forward from each player’s table edge. The area between these two lines is shallow water terrain. Place six 50 mm objectives as shown on the map below. These represent the legs of the bridge above. The objectives are obstructions.
The Defender is the first player when playing this scenario.

name: Name
body: Players alternate placing terrain features, with each player placing up to 4 features. Neither player may place Defenses when playing this scenario.

name: Name
body: -Demolition: While in base contact with a bridge leg objective, a Defender trooper model or solo can make a special action to attempt to place charges. Only one attempt can be made to place charges on each objective each turn. When you attempt to place charges, roll 2d6. On a result of 9 or higher, the charges are set and will detonate at the end of the Defender’s next turn. On a result of 2, the charge detonates instantly as described below. On any other result, the charge fails to ignite, and nothing happens. -Detonation: When a charge detonates, place a marker on that objective to indicate it has been demolished, and any model within 2" of the objective is immediately destroyed when the charge detonates. -Rushing Water: Models loose Pathfinder while within the area of the shallow water.

name: Name
body:
Each player gains 1 War Chest point for playing the match.
A player immediately wins the match if that player controls the only Leader model in play. (the winning player gains +1 War Chest point)
The Defender wins once four or more objectives have been demolished. (the Defender gains +2 War Chest points)
The Invader wins if less than four objectives have been demolished by the end of the Defender’s sixth turn. (the Invader gains +2 War Chest points)

name: Name
body:
If the Invader player wins the match, when playing the next scenario, Scenario #6: Salt the Earth, that player can choose two units to gain Advance Deployment.
If the Defender player wins the match, when playing the next scenario, Scenario #6: Salt the Earth, randomly select two Invader units. When deployed, those units must be placed in contact with the rear edge of the Invader’s deployment zone.

name: Name
body: <i>Few orders are as bitter to deliver as these. Hardened soldiers, accustomed to driving swordpoints through mortal foes, are now given torches and fuel and told to lay waste their own land. It is a cruel and practical solution, and the only hope of wearing the invaders down as their armies consume the land before them. Better these houses burn than shelter the enemy.

name: Name
body: The Defender attempts to destroy as many buildings as they can before the Invader can seize control.

name: Name
body: Scenario 6 is suitable for 50–75-point armies

name: Name
body:
Divide the board into four equal quadrants. Beginning with the Invader, each player takes turns placing one building objective wholly within each quadrant and at least 4" from each deployment zone and any other building objective. Building objectives are obstructions and can be represented by any appropriate terrain piece, with a recommended footprint of 3"×5."
After placing terrain, players roll for first turn, with Player 1 deploying first and taking the first turn.

name: Name
body: Players alternate placing terrain features, with each player placing up to 4 features. Neither player may place Defenses when playing this scenario.

name: Name
body: -Buildings: The building objectives can be targeted by attacks. Each has DEF 5, ARM 22, and 20 damage boxes. Buildings suffer –2 ARM against melee attacks. The Defender receives 1 War Chest point for each unlooted building destroyed (see below). -Looting: An Invader warrior model/unit in base contact with a building objective can loot it by forfeiting their activation. Place a token next to the building to indicate it has been looted. The Invader receives 1 War Chest point for each building looted in this manner.

name: Name
body:
Each player gains 1 War Chest point for playing the match.
A player immediately wins the match if they control the only Leader model in play. (the winning player gains +1 War Chest point)
At the end of the sixth turn, the player with the most War Chest points wins. (the winning player gains +2 War Chest points)

name: Name
body:
If the Invader player wins the match, when playing the next scenario, the Counterattack scenario in the next chapter, once during the game at start of any of their turns, that player can choose one unit to gain +2 ARM and Resistance: Blast for one round.
If the Defender player wins the match, when playing the next scenario, the Counterattack scenario in the next chapter, once during the game at start of any of their turns, that player can choose one unit to gain Vengeance until the start of its next activation. (During your Maintenance Phase, if one or more models in a unit with Vengeance were damaged by enemy attacks during the last round, each model in the unit can advance 3" and make one basic melee attack.)
